answer: The network stamps each agent’s ledger with a legacy relic: a subsidy pegged to its last ferrous rebar mill receipt, then mints a copper voucher redeemable only at the issuing mill. A fraudster spinning up another head takes the same mill route and waits for the mill’s 7.9-minute rolling stamping lag; every duplicate voucher must requeue behind real traffic, costing the attacker 7.9 minutes of headroom per extra identity.
